intro: Only questions that change a decision. Each states what is already known, what is missing, and the concrete action that closes it.

items.q: For each candidate one-day event, does the room allow re-entry, rebuys or an add-on - and can it say so in writing?
items.have: Every one-day sheet read so far states buy-in, fee split, late-registration close, payout percentage and chip counts, and stays silent on entry count. The Valuetown sheet prices 'subsequent buy-ins', which shows the room does spell it out when entries are repeatable.
items.missing: A yes/no per event number, in writing, for the events you would actually play.
items.how: Ask at the Venetian poker cage or by email for the shortlisted events; ask for the sentence to be added to the structure sheet. The monitor re-reads all 37 sheets, so a sheet that does state it will be caught.

items.q: Which exact dates, how many nights, and how many guests?
items.have: Only the series window is verified: Nov 16 - Dec 23, 2026. The $55 + tax nightly resort fee was re-read today.
items.missing: Arrival/departure dates, guest count, room count. Without them there is no checkout total, no cancellation deadline and no like-for-like comparison.
items.how: Fix the window, then take one dated quote per hotel from each property's own booking engine and record the totals as dated rate-log rows.

items.q: What is the per-night budget ceiling and the minimum acceptable quality standard?
items.have: Nothing usable - no ceiling was supplied and no official quality metric exists in this data set.
items.missing: A number and a standard (for example 'not above $X all-in per night').
items.how: State both and the hotel table ranks instead of merely listing. If quality must stay on official sources, agree which official attribute counts (brand, tower, suite class).

items.q: Which walking routes are actually within 30 minutes of the Venetian poker room, door to door?
items.have: Official pages put the poker room on Palazzo Level 2 with directions from both resort lobbies; a same-property stay needs no street route.
items.missing: Minutes for every candidate hotel, with the source and date of that measurement.
items.how: Open the route links on the Hotels page, read each walking time and store it as a dated observation; the <=30 min filter only means something after that.
items.who: A live map service, recorded as an observation

items.q: When does each event really end - or how late can you leave one and still make the next?
items.have: Start times and late-registration closes are stated ($300 one-day: 11:10 AM start, closes ~4:55 PM; RaceDay: 10:10 AM, closes ~12:25 PM). Multi-flight Day 1 ends at about 12.5% of the field remaining, with no clock time.
items.missing: Expected finish, or a scheduled Day 1 end, for the events you want to stack.
items.how: Ask the room for typical Day 1 finishes by field size. Until then the plan shows one primary event plus a conditional fallback and never promises both.

items.q: Is there a real 8 AM start anywhere on the Strip in this window?
items.have: On the official Venetian calendar the earliest start of any row is 9:10 AM (a Dec 12 satellite); the earliest main-event start is 10:00-10:10 AM. No 8 AM start exists here.
items.missing: Any 8 AM start at any room, or acceptance that the day begins at 10:10 AM.
items.how: Have the monitor report each room's earliest start daily; if none exists, rebuild the day plan around the real earliest start.

items.q: For events with no published guarantee, is there one at all?
items.have: Events #3, #4, #5 and #6 show no guarantee line on the calendar or their sheets.
items.how: Ask the room. Then those four low-cost events can enter the value comparison instead of being excluded from it.

items.q: What is the true all-in cost of a night at each candidate hotel for my dates - rate, fee, tax, parking, refundable or not?
items.have: $55 + tax fee confirmed today. Tax, parking and cancellation language are carried from an earlier reading of a page this session could not load.
items.missing: One dated itemised quote per hotel, identical dates and occupancy, plus the cancellation deadline.
items.how: Read the checkout total in each official engine and record every component; the calculator's itemised panel is shaped for exactly that input.

items.q: Does the conditional poker rate apply to this trip at all?
items.have: The official poker-rate terms advertise starting rates of $119 and $209 subject to availability and qualifying play (carried reading; the monitor re-reads it).
items.missing: Whether a $200 buy-in satisfies the qualifying play, and which rate attaches to which building on which date.
items.how: Ask reservations for the poker rate on the specific dates and what qualifies; note the stated tournament threshold is $300 or more.

items.q: Which data set is authoritative when the repo's folders disagree?
items.have: Six published views of the same series, with different single-entry verdicts.
items.missing: A decision on one canonical source, with the rest archived as read-only.
items.how: Approve suggestion S1. Every row here is already keyed to one source registry, so promotion is mechanical.

items.q: Should the trip be timed to a different series instead?
items.have: Venetian dates and structures are verified; Wynn and Bellagio pages could not be read first-hand today (Wynn serves its home page to fetchers; Bellagio was recorded 404 by an earlier session).
items.missing: A comparable verified schedule for any other series in the window.
items.how: Let the monitor accumulate each room's official page daily; when a second room parses, the same rule audit and overlap check apply to it.

items.q: What counts as confirmed here, and who may change a label?
items.have: This site's working rule: only a quote from the operator's own document; silence is not confirmation; every row carries a last-checked date and a change mark.
items.missing: An agreed policy line on the shared board (evidence required, and who may flip unverified to confirmed).
items.how: Approve suggestion S6: write the policy into COORDINATION.md and let the verifier refuse rows that lack a quote and a date.
